s: From earlier goodby, Godby, Godby'e, Godbwye, God b'w'y, God bwy yee, God buy you, God be wi' you, each a progressively shorter contraction of God be with ye or God be with you. Note the change of God to good by confusion with good morning, good night, etc.

t: Goodbye or good-bye? | WordReference Forums
s: May 10, 2006 - As alahay noted (post 11), the word/phrase has undergone some change: 14th century: God be with ye Fused in the 16th century: Godbwye (various spellings: God be wy you, god b'w'y, godbwye, god buy' ye, and good-b'wy) Influenced by 'good morning', 'good night': Good-by And thence to good-bye and goodbye.
